clue.text: Small tip: books tell us lots

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a peak is the tip or top of a mountain
volumes are books

explanation.surface: Someone passes on a little advice: these books have a great deal to say.
explanation.walkthrough: The colon makes 'Small tip' look like a heading for a piece of advice; it is really S plus a synonym for a summit.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: something that reveals a great deal without words is said to do this, so it tells us plenty.

clue.text: Buy tea, going into wallet

indicators.note: going into says the word for tea is placed inside the word for wallet

parts.note: a purse is a small wallet for money
cha (or char) is British slang for tea

explanation.surface: A shopper buys a cup of tea and puts the change back in the wallet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going into' sets the tea word inside the wallet word; British slang spells tea as cha or char.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to buy something is to acquire it by payment, as a verb, matching the noun-free sense of 'Buy'.

clue.text: A queen, gracious host

parts.note: R stands for Regina, Latin for queen
'my!' and 'gracious!' are both exclamations of surprise

explanation.surface: A queen is praised as a gracious hostess at a royal reception.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gracious' is read as the exclamation 'Gracious!', which MY can replace ('My!'). 'host' is not the person entertaining but a great multitude.
explanation.definitionFit: A host is a large crowd or multitude, and the word once meant specifically an armed force, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: One making choice to keep broken metal item of circuitry

indicators.note: to keep says the voter holds the rearranged word inside

parts.note: a voter is someone making a choice at the ballot box

indicators.note: broken says the letters of metal are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone choosing between gadgets holds on to a broken metal part from an electric circuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges the letters of 'metal', and 'to keep' has the voter word hold that mixture after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an electrolytic instrument placed in a circuit to measure the quantity of electric charge passing through it.

clue.text: Chance to share small room with relative

parts.note: loo is British slang for a toilet, often a small room
kin are relatives, family members

explanation.surface: Someone gets the opportunity to share a little room with a family member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small room' is the toilet, a common euphemism: LOO is British informal for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal noun for an opportunity to take part in something, as in getting a fair turn or involvement.

clue.text: Damage most of monarch's tent

parts.note: to mar is to damage or spoil

indicators.note: most of says the word for the monarch loses its last letter

parts.note: a queen is a monarch; the 's is just possessive surface

explanation.surface: Vandals damage most of the king's or queen's royal tent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' drops the final letter of the monarch word.
explanation.definitionFit: A large tent used for outdoor events such as weddings and garden parties; a specific type of tent.

clue.text: Roadside observers a Merc passed travelling around Spain

indicators.note: around says the rearranged letters wrap the letter for Spain
travelling says the letters of the phrase move about into a new order

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

explanation.surface: Roadside watchers note a Mercedes passing them as it drives round Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travelling' rearranges A MERC PASSED, and 'around' puts that mix round E (Spain's car code).
explanation.definitionFit: Devices mounted beside roads that photograph speeding vehicles, so they keep watch on passing traffic.

clue.text: A Zulu in severe danger

indicators.note: in says the letter pair sits inside the word for severe

parts.note: hard means severe, as in a hard winter
Zulu is the NATO phonetic alphabet word for Z

explanation.surface: A Zulu warrior finds himself in grave peril.
explanation.walkthrough: Zulu stands for Z in the radio alphabet; A and Z go inside HARD.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a risk or peril is a source of danger, and the word is used for both.

clue.text: Broadcast on fine trade show

indicators.note: on says the word for broadcast is placed after the abbreviation for fine

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
to air a programme is to broadcast it

explanation.surface: A trade exhibition is broadcast on a fine day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' wants to be a homophone signal, but it is AIR; 'on' sets it after F.
explanation.definitionFit: A fair is an exhibition where businesses display goods, as in a book fair or trade fair.

clue.text: Spice Girl content in journey somewhere in Australia

parts.note: Mel B (Melanie Brown) was one of the Spice Girls pop group

indicators.note: content in says to take the inside letters of journey, losing its ends

explanation.surface: A former pop star is happy during a trip somewhere Down Under.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content' looks like 'happy' but means the contents: the middle of jOURNEy, OURNE. Mel B was 'Scary Spice' in the 1990s Spice Girls.
explanation.definitionFit: Melbourne is the capital of the state of Victoria, a major city in Australia, so it is an example.

clue.text: Bearing cost about fiver in the end, without delivery charge

parts.note: carriage is the way one holds oneself, one's bearing

indicators.note: about says the word for cost goes round a letter

parts.note: a fee is a cost or charge

indicators.note: in the end says to take the final letter of fiver

explanation.surface: Someone shoulders the cost of about five pounds, eventually avoiding any postage charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bearing' looks like 'carrying' but means posture; 'about' wraps the cost word round R, which 'in the end' takes from fiver.
explanation.definitionFit: Carriage here means the cost of transporting goods, so goods sent with that cost waived arrive free of postage.

clue.text: Indifference in course in outskirts of Aylesbury

indicators.note: in says the word for course goes inside the edge letters
outskirts of says to take only the outer letters of Aylesbury

parts.note: a path is a course or route

explanation.surface: Someone shows indifference on a course at the edge of Aylesbury, an English market town.
explanation.walkthrough: Aylesbury is a town in Buckinghamshire, England; its outskirts are A and Y, with PATH between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a lack of interest, enthusiasm or concern is indifference.

clue.text: Plump guide sadly exhausted

parts.note: fat means plump

indicators.note: sadly signals that the letters of guide are in a poor, jumbled state

explanation.surface: A tubby tour guide is sadly worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' rearranges the letters of 'guide' into IGUED.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: being worn out through effort is being tired, weary and exhausted.

clue.text: Have cold in shelter on High Street, or thereabouts

indicators.note: in says the words for have and cold sit inside the shelter

parts.note: a tent is a shelter
to own is to have
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
re means on or concerning, as in a letter heading

explanation.surface: Someone with a cold takes shelter in a tent on the high street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' gives RE as in 'regarding'. 'High Street' is the British name for a town's main shopping street.
explanation.definitionFit: The main shopping street is at or near the central part of a town, hence the hedged 'or thereabouts'.

clue.text: Again find sample of Everywhere: disco version

indicators.note: sample of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A DJ samples a disco remix of a song called 'Everywhere'.
explanation.definitionFit: To come upon something lost or forgotten for a second time is to find it anew, a direct verb equivalent.

clue.text: Gamble on a character from Greece

parts.note: a bet is a gamble

explanation.surface: Someone places a wager on a Greek person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'character' looks like a person but is a letter of the Greek alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Beta is the second letter of the Greek alphabet, and a letter is a written character.

clue.text: Studious learner involved in editing novel

indicators.note: involved in says the learner letter is wrapped up inside the other letters
novel means new, so the letters of editing take a new form

parts.note: L is for learner, as on British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: A conscientious trainee is busy editing a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book, but signals rearranging EDITING, with L inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone who is studious is hard-working, careful and conscientious in study.

clue.text: Reptiles like empty places

parts.note: as means like, as in 'white as snow'

indicators.note: empty says places is emptied of its middle, keeping only its outer letters

explanation.surface: Snakes tend to favour deserted spots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'like' is not the verb but the comparison word AS; 'empty' leaves P and S from places.
explanation.definitionFit: Asps are small venomous snakes, and snakes are reptiles, so these are an example of the class.

clue.text: Ran through coastal structure erected last month

parts.note: a pier is a structure projecting from the coast into the sea

indicators.note: erected in a down clue means built upward, so the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: Dec is the abbreviation for December, the last month of the year

explanation.surface: A seaside pier was put up last month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'erected' turns DEC upward in this down clue, giving CED below PIER.
explanation.definitionFit: To run something through, as with a sword or spike, is to stab or pierce it, so the past tenses match.

clue.text: Hell uncovered during show that's unseemly

indicators.note: during says the uncovered letters go within the word for show

parts.note: to indicate is to show or point out

indicators.note: uncovered says Hell loses its outer letters, its covering

explanation.surface: A performance with hellish material is condemned as improper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncovered' strips the outer letters of 'Hell', and 'during' places what is left within the show word.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: tactless, coarse or improper behaviour is unseemly.

clue.text: Business acquiring clubs in New York after some time

indicators.note: after says the New York piece is placed following the word for time

parts.note: an age is a period of time

indicators.note: in says the clubs letter goes inside the New York letters

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs, the card suit

explanation.surface: A company takes over some nightclubs in New York after a while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clubs' is the card suit, C, not nightclubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an agency is a company or firm providing a service, such as a travel or advertising business.

clue.text: Big cat's junior imbibing water in Spain

indicators.note: imbibing means drinking in, so the junior letters take the water inside

parts.note: agua is Spanish for water

explanation.surface: A young big cat drinks water while in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'cat's' stands for 'is', linking definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The jaguar is a large spotted wild feline of the Americas, one of the big cats.

clue.text: Delighted to welcome European, very lofty

indicators.note: to welcome means to take in, so the delighted word holds the other letters

parts.note: elated means delighted

explanation.surface: Someone is thrilled to greet a European of very high standing.
explanation.walkthrough: E and V go inside ELATED after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something high up or of high rank is lofty, raised and exalted.

clue.text: Regularly action team attached to a leisure venue

indicators.note: regularly says to take every other letter of action team

explanation.surface: An action team is regularly sent to a sports and leisure centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' takes the second, fourth and so on letters of aCtIoN tEaM, giving CINEM.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture house is a place people visit to watch films in their free time, so it is an example.

clue.text: Real regret after end of engagement

indicators.note: after says the word for regret follows the final letter
end of says to take the final letter of engagement

parts.note: to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: Genuine sorrow after a broken-off engagement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of engagement' looks like a break-up; it is just the letter T.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something genuine or authentic is real, not fake.

clue.text: Scout I note runs, following sport on playing field

indicators.note: on says the sport comes after the playing field
following says the next letters come after the sport

parts.note: rec is British short for recreation ground, a public playing field
RU stands for rugby union
te is a note in tonic sol-fa (do re mi fa so la te)
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A talent scout notes a player's runs while watching sport on the playing field.
explanation.walkthrough: REC is the British 'rec', the local recreation ground; RU is rugby union.
explanation.definitionFit: A talent scout seeks out promising players or staff to sign up, which is a recruiter's role.

clue.text: Burn boat after king's left

indicators.note: left here means gone away, so the king letter is removed

parts.note: a ketch is a two-masted sailing boat
K is the chess abbreviation for king; the 's stands for 'has'

explanation.surface: Someone sets fire to a boat once the king has departed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'king's left' is 'king has left': K departs KETCH.
explanation.definitionFit: To etch is to engrave by corroding a surface with acid, so it can be likened to burning into metal.

clue.text: Send one terms about driving offence records

indicators.note: about says the letters of the three words are turned around into a new order

explanation.surface: An official sends someone the terms relating to their motoring convictions.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, driving offences are recorded on a licence as these, with penalty points.
explanation.definitionFit: In UK law, these are records of motoring convictions noted on a driving licence.
